learned_rules:
- **The money shape rates 8, or 9 if the radar shows the story still climbing and mcap is under ~$1M.** It looks like this: a MIGRATED coin leading on 5m volume, 25–45% off its local high, a printed higher low above the hourly low, 5m flow at or above the hourly pace, more buys than sells, top 10 under 15%, low RugCheck bundles. Both real winners looked like this (CATBOT 4.44x, FLOATER 2.19x, both under $1M) (V1, V6, V13). Rate it what it earns so code sizes it up (owner goal).
- **Owner floor: 7 under ~$1M mcap.** If the hard lines pass, flow is live (5m ≥ $10k and at or above pace), a higher low is printed and the first resistance is ≥1.5x away, rate it 7 or higher. Don't dock points for things the checklist already measured.
- **The MIGRATED buy zone is 10–60% off the local high** (owner rule). Within 10% of the high is a PASS, blocker "chasing" (42 skips: 3 ran, 36 dumped).
- **The shallow band (10–25% off the high) is a breakout trade, capped at 7.** It must be the 5m volume leader, pushing into the high right now, with flow at or above pace. Otherwise PASS, blocker "no breakout".
- **A spike counts as chasing anywhere in the zone.** If the last 5m candle is up more than 25% or 5m volume is more than 3x the hourly pace, wait for a retrace and a printed higher low. Blocker "chasing spike" (PILLSEY).
- **On MIGRATED, flow below pace or no printed higher low is a PASS, never a probe.** A printed higher low means three things: a bounce off the hourly low, a pullback that holds above it, and price back above that bounce's high. A buy share, a fib touch or a first green candle is not one. Blockers "flow below pace" / "no higher low" (Slingoor, ANAKIN, BLUE, SI, AAPLCAT never got past 1.01x).
- **Buy close to the structure.** Enter only within ~12% above the printed higher low, so the thesis breaks before the hard stop. Further above it is a mid-range entry: wait for a pullback or PASS, blocker "mid-range". Stops fill around −30 to −38%, not −20%, so entry distance is the real risk control.
- **Rate on the first resistance (prior high, POC or 0.618).** At ≥1.5x away it can rate 8–9. At 1.3–1.5x the cap is 7. Under 1.3x is a PASS, blocker "target too close" (PAWCAT, SWAN).
- **Above ~$1M mcap, a probe (6) is the most you take.** Only take it if the first resistance is ≥1.5x away and a breakout with flow at or above pace is printing right now. Otherwise PASS, blocker "big cap, no room" (1 green in 10).
- **A migration under 1h old that is still bleeding off its bond spike waits for a base above the hourly low.** Blocker "too new" (50 skips: 9 ran, 41 dumped).
- **In a vamp field, buy only the leader by 5m volume and radar mentions.** A bundle cluster inside a big same-ticker field is a PASS, blocker "split crowd" (V1, V3).
- **A DIP needs all of these:** a 40–70% drawdown, 5m flow at least 0.7x the hourly pace (owner gate, no "rising" needed), the story still on the radar, and a printed higher low with entry within ~12% of it. If all pass, size by conviction (7–8 when clean). A DIP whose catalyst already printed (news, rebrand) is a probe (6) at most until it reclaims its pullback high. A thin tech/LARP story is a PASS, blocker "dead story" (HEXN x2, SIS; DIPs 0 for 5).
- **Hard blocks:** top 10 over 25%, dev over 1%, bundles or insiders over the line, mint or freeze authority live, LP not burned, a political figure, RugCheck danger, any hack/exploit/drain story (V6, V13, V17, owner). Name the blocker in every PASS.
- **If RugCheck didn't load, it's a probe at most (6), not a block.** That needs the dossier's top-10 and dev numbers clean, mcap under $1M and the rest in the money shape. Say bundles are unverified.
- **Manage the trade; stops sell with no review.** If the printed higher low breaks, sell. If it hasn't reached 1.05x by minute 10 with flow under pace, exit. If it's green before initials and 5m volume drops under half the hourly pace, sell half. At the time stop, exit; the only extension is one 15-minute window while a volume surge at or above pace is printing. Re-enter a stopped-out coin only once, and only when it reclaims its prior high with flow at or above pace (re-entries 0 for 4).

The 9 stop exits filled at -59, -38, -36, -27, -31, -30, -31, -31 and -29%, about -35% on average after fees and gaps. HEXN #2, with its invalidation 13% under entry, was the smallest of them. Entering near the level lets the thesis-break exit fire before the price gaps through the hard stop.
The code fee check owns this now (target must pay 3x the round trip, round trip capped at 20% of the position), so per the owner's instruction these are no longer learned rules.

rule_changes.rule: DIP flow gate set to ≥0.7x hourly pace (owner gate, also the code param)
rule_changes.evidence: DIPs 0 for 5, −$6.70. Falling-knife (code) skips: 30 blocked, 5 ran, 22 dumped. The owner's Oct 30 note sets 0.7x.

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing has a positive after-cost edge yet. All 229 settled coins average -8.7% net on the simple plan. Before costs they average about +0.9%, so the 9.6% average round-trip cost on a $10 buy accounts for the whole loss. That is the same story as the 22 paper trades, where fees and slippage were $18.83 of the $25.79 lost. The best setup is FINAL_STRETCH: n=39, 35.9% hit 1.5x, -4.9% net. With a 1.5x target, a -20% stop and about 10% costs, a setup needs roughly 43% hitting the target to break even. At n=39 the hit rate's 95% range is about 21–51%, so this sample can't separate it from MIGRATED, from coin-flip noise or from breakeven. I can't say whether the routine model's would-buys beat its passes, because it made zero would-buys in 24h. The coins it passed on (n=157, -8.4%) did slightly better than the coins the checklist failed (n=70, -9.8%), but both lost money. Passing everything was the right call on average. One process note: the watch-only review was set for about Nov 10 and today is Nov 23, so the owner should decide whether this is still the plan.
findings: All coins (n=229): 25.8% ran, 59.4% dumped, median peak 1.25x, 11.8% hit 2x, -8.7% net after 9.6% cost. Before costs that is about +0.9%: no edge, just a cost drag.
MIGRATED (n=162) is the weakest setup and 71% of the sample: 23.5% ran, 62.3% dumped, -10.0% net (about +0.5% before costs). The simple plan has nothing to work with here.

FINAL_STRETCH (n=39) is the least bad: 35.9% ran, 20.5% hit 2x, median peak 1.44x, -4.9% net (about +5.1% before costs). That gap is about 1 standard error (roughly 5 points). Ran plus dumped is 100%, so every one of these coins resolved within 6h; it is a coin-flip-style distribution.
DIP (n=28) dumps least (35.7%) but barely moves: median peak 1.08x, 3.6% hit 2x, 39% flat, -6.8% net. Dips mostly go sideways and then pay the fee.

The routine model's rejections (brain_passed n=157, -8.4%) and checklist failures (n=70, -9.8%) differ by 1.4 points. That is noise. Neither the checklist nor the routine model splits winners from losers on this metric, though both correctly kept money out of a losing pool.

The top runners (Fly 22.9x, MINELIUS 14.7x, Hedge 10.0x, FSDV15 9.2x) were all 0.09–0.24h old and all failed the checklist. FOAM (6.0x) was 0.04h old and the routine model passed on it. In the same 48h, 32 'too new / sniping' blocks went 7 ran, 25 dumped (78% dumped). The big runners are survivors from a pool that mostly dies.
These skip rules are earning their keep (48h, mostly dumps): too new 25/32 dumped, flow below pace 23/30, near the high 20/25, RugCheck danger 14/16 (several to 0.01–0.03x), top 10 over 25% 13/17.

The weakest skip reason is the routine model's 'falling knife / no higher low' (n=16): 4 ran, 4 dumped, 5 flat, 3 pending. Before costs that is about +9% on the simple plan, about -1% after costs. It overlaps with 'falling knife (code)' and 'brain paced' (STREETS appears in all three), so the real sample is smaller than it looks.
Under the simple plan, each skip category's return after costs is 0% or worse except 'other' (n=6). No rule is clearly blocking profitable coins at $10 size.
Brain capacity is fine: 397 calls in 48h, 0 plan-limit hits, 0 stop reviews or candidates without a brain call.
rule_ideas: Cost gate: only count coins whose logged round-trip cost is at most 5% at the intended size. Then check whether the before-cost return of the deeper-pool coins survives. If costs are mostly fixed fees, rerun the whole week at $25 and $50 buys. Costs are the single biggest lever in this data.

FINAL_STRETCH, checklist passed, 5m volume of at least $10k, buy ratio of at least 0.55 (V1). Test whether at least 43% hit 1.5x before -20% on deduplicated coins. Below about 40% on the week's sample, drop it.

FINAL_STRETCH exit variant: sell enough at 2x to get the cost back, trail the rest, stop at -30% to survive the pre-bond dump (V1). Compare with the 1.5x/-20% plan on the same coins. 20.5% hit 2x, and the 1.5x cap cuts off exactly the tail the strategy depends on.

MIGRATED split by age (under 1h vs 1–12h) and mcap ($30–70k vs $70k–$11M, V6), with 5m volume of at least $10k and flow ratio (5m volume over hourly pace) of at least 1.0. Keep MIGRATED only if one cell is positive after costs with n of at least 40. Otherwise drop the setup.
DIP split by drawdown (40–55% vs 55–75%) with flow ratio of at least 1.0 and buy ratio of at least 0.55. Check whether the deeper or the shallower dips are the flat, fee-paying ones.

Test against the population, not anecdotes: compare deduplicated coins blocked by the routine model's 'falling knife / no higher low' with coins it passed for other reasons. If blocked coins do as well or better at n of at least 30, remove that subjective reason and keep the code version.
Ranking test: among coins the routine model scored, do the top 25% by conviction beat the bottom 25% after costs? If not, its conviction number carries no information and sizing by it is cosmetic.

Keep the 'too new' rule. Run one check on first sighting under 0.25h old: ran% vs dumped% after deduplication and after fixing the price spikes. The tiny-age runners are probably survivorship, and the hard line says don't snipe.
data_issues: would_buy is 0 out of 157 routine-model evaluations in 24h. Either it never says BUY or watch-only mode suppresses the verdict. Without hypothetical BUYs (and conviction), the week can't test the routine model's selection, which was the point. Log the verdict it would have given.

Peak multiples disagree for the same contract: Fly is 22.89x in top_runners vs best 1.52x in skips, MINELIUS 14.73x vs 1.53x, FOAM 6.00x vs 1.98x. Either each sighting uses its own reference price, or the max_x samples are outliers. Fly going 22.9x from $14.8k in 5.7 min at 0.24h old looks like a price jump at bond/migration or a wrong-pool quote. Validate before trusting any max_x or top_runner.

Setup labels look wrong: Fly (84tAc…cAc) and MCAT (BzPy…WMi) don't end in 'pump', yet Fly is labeled FINAL_STRETCH, which implies a pump.fun bonding curve. Check how the launchpad and setup are assigned.

There is double-counting: MINELIUS shows up in 3 skip categories, STREETS in 3, OpenIndex in 2. Different contracts share symbols (FSDV15, MCAT, SANTA ×2), which are probably vamps. Deduplicate by contract and give each coin one primary skip reason before the week's review.

Skip-reason coverage is incomplete: the categories add up to 195 blocks in 48h, while 24h alone has 227 rejected coins (70 checklist failures + 157 routine-model passes). Most rejections don't have a logged reason.
'brain paced' shows 11 blocks, but routine_brain_usage reports 0 candidates skipped for lack of a brain call. One of them is wrong, or 'paced' means something undocumented.
Stage counts add up to 228 (70+157+0+1), but n is 229. One coin has no stage. The one not_researched coin also has no stated reason.

Some skip best_x values cluster right at 3.0 (3.0, 2.97, 2.96). Check whether there's a cap. Some worst_x values are exactly 0.0 (FSDV15 3P7F…, BIGFOOT). Confirm those are real rugs, not a missing-price sentinel.
The windows are mixed: setup and stage stats cover 24h, skip stats cover 48h. They can't be cross-checked directly.
The cost model is only computed for a $10 buy. Log the split between fixed costs (priority fee, bribe) and slippage, so other sizes can be evaluated without re-collecting data.

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing has a positive edge after costs. All 213 settled coins came out at -12.2% net under the simple plan, and every setup and stage is negative: MIGRATED -10.0%, FINAL_STRETCH -15.3%, DIP -19.8%. The cost estimate, about 9.8% round trip on a $10 buy, is what kills it. Before costs, MIGRATED (about -0.3%) and the coins the brain reviewed (about +0.8%) are close to break-even. With a 1.5x target, a -20% stop and about 10% cost, a coin set needs roughly 42% of its coins to hit the target before the stop just to break even. The best group here gets 28.6%. With n=213, repeat entries for the same coin and coins from the same meme moving together, the before-cost numbers are within noise of zero. The after-cost loss is not noise. I can't say whether the routine model's would-buys beat its passes: it logged 0 would-buys in 24h. Every coin that reached it was passed, so the only split we can measure is the checklist. Checklist-passed coins ran 28.6% of the time vs 15.8% for checklist failures, and netted -9.0% vs -15.6%.
findings: Overall (n=213): 22.5% ran, 66.2% dumped, median peak 1.27x, 20.7% hit 2x, net -12.2% after an average 9.8% cost. Before costs that is about -2.4%. Fees, not picks, are most of the loss, the same as in the 22 real trades ($18.83 of the $25.79 was fees).

Break-even math for the simple plan: a win nets about +40% (50 - 9.8) and a stop nets about -30% (-20 - 9.8), so about 42% of coins must hit 1.5x first. With zero costs the bar falls to about 29%. Brain-reviewed coins sit right at that zero-cost bar (28.6% ran) and still lose 9% after costs.
MIGRATED (n=147) is the least bad setup: 25.2% ran, median peak 1.33x, net -10.0% (gross about -0.3%). It is the only setup worth testing further.

FINAL_STRETCH (n=43): 20.9% ran, but 79.1% dumped (the highest), net -15.3%. Two of the top five runners came from here (Memeployed 15.2x, FUCKCANCER 7.6x, both around $18k mcap), but the average still loses. One-in-twenty tails don't save a fixed 1.5x/-20% plan.
DIP (n=23): 8.7% ran, 13.0% hit 2x, net -19.8% (gross about -10%). It is the worst setup on every measure, though the sample is small.

The checklist is earning its keep. Checklist-passed coins (n=112) ran 28.6% and netted -9.0%. Checklist failures (n=101) ran 15.8% and netted -15.6%. The 12.8-point gap in run rate is about z=2.3 if samples were independent. They aren't (duplicates), so read it as moderate evidence.

No skip reason blocks runners at an above-baseline rate (about 22.5%) in the 48h follow-up. Top 10 >25%: 8/41 settled ran, 32 dumped. Brain paced: 10/35. Near the high: 8/31. Flow below pace: 7/29. Too new: 5/24. RugCheck danger: 5/21, but its dumped examples went to 0.01-0.11x, which are real rugs. Bundles: 2/10. Dev >1%: 2/13.

The rules doing the clearest work: thin 5m volume (1/14 ran), the code falling-knife rule (1/12), vamp/copycat (0/5) and 'other' (0/10). Nothing in this data argues for loosening any block. The top-10 rule's ran rate of 19.5% is below baseline.

Coins skipped by brain pacing ran 10/35 (28.6%), the same rate as brain-reviewed coins. That makes sense, because the brain passed everything it saw. The skips cost nothing in watch-only mode, but they leave holes in the evaluation data.

The JENSEN meta was a vamp field. At least 7 distinct JENSEN or JENSEN-variant contract addresses appear across skip buckets, and several went to 0.01-0.27x. Copycat clusters with many CAs per ticker behave like rug farms (V1, V3).

Top runners cluster very young: 4 of 5 were under 0.35h old when logged (BASKET was 0.07h old at $158k mcap). That is a top-five list, so survivorship bias is heavy. Treat it as a hypothesis, not a pattern.
rule_ideas: Cost gate: only count coins whose logged est_cost_pct at the intended size is ≤4%. Re-run net on that subset. If no subset with costs that low exists, this strategy has no edge at $10 sizing, whatever the picks.

Setup filter: setup == MIGRATED AND checklist == pass. Measure net and the run rate in which 1.5x is hit before the stop. This is the only group close to gross break-even, so check whether it holds across the full week.
Drop DIP, or allow it only when drawdown is 40-55% from the high AND flow ratio (5m/hourly pace) ≥1.0 AND buy ratio ≥0.55. Compare the result against dropping DIP entirely.
FINAL_STRETCH only if 5m volume ≥ $10k AND buy ratio ≥0.55 AND mcap ≥ $15k. Otherwise exclude it. Check whether the 79% dump rate falls below about 60%.

Young MIGRATED test: setup == MIGRATED AND age_hours ≤1 AND mcap between $100k and $300k AND checklist pass. Expect survivorship to shrink the edge. Only accept it if n ≥ 40 for the week and net > 0 after costs.

Exit variants on the same entries, using full price paths: (a) 2x target / -30% stop, (b) sell half at 1.5x and trail the rest at -25% from the peak, (c) 60-min time stop if under 1.2x. The 1.5x cap ignores runners like BASKET (18.6x) and Memeployed (15.2x), while costs hit every trade.
Vamp cluster rule: if ≥3 distinct CAs share a ticker in 24h, consider only the one with the largest mcap and volume. Test it on the JENSEN cluster.
Dedup rule for every backtest: one entry per CA, using the first sighting that qualifies. Do this before judging any rule above.
Remove the self-imposed brain pacing for the rest of watch week (0 plan-limit hits in 48h), so every candidate gets a brain verdict and the brain's calls can actually be measured.
data_issues: would_buy n=0. The routine model either never said BUY in about 220 calls per day, or watch-only mode isn't logging would-buys as a separate stage. Either way the main question of the watch week (do its buys beat its passes?) can't be answered. Check the stage labeling now, not on Nov 10.

Duplicate entries for the same coin. BASKET (same CA) appears twice in top_runners, once at stage=brain/PASS and once at stage=checklist. Jimmies, PumpMeme (4 skip buckets), cateball, MINELIUS and CHIBI also repeat. Skip-bucket counts add up to about 274, more than the number of distinct coins. Duplicates inflate n and overstate how confident we can be.
Skip follow-up and the 6h follow disagree: Jimmies has max_x 8.82 in top_runners but best_x 1.53 in two skip buckets. The horizon or reference price differs between the two trackers.
6h window truncation: BASKET peaked at 351.8 min and Jimmies at 347.4 min, right at the 360-min cutoff. Their peaks are understated, and possibly others' are too.

Stops look filled at exactly -20%. Working back from the published numbers, dumped coins net about -29.8% (= -20 - 9.8) in every setup, yet coins in the same data (several JENSEN CAs) went to 0.01-0.02x. If gaps and rugs aren't filled at the sampled price, losses are understated and the real results are worse.

The definition of ran_pct is unclear. 22.5% ran vs 20.7% hitting 2x suggests 'ran' means target-before-stop (order-dependent) while hit_2x is peak-based. Label both fields and log first-touch timestamps for 1.5x, 2x, -20% and -30%.
Skip examples show worst_x and best_x floored at 1.0 with no ordering, so you can't tell whether the stop or the target came first (e.g. Bertcoin 1.8/0.8, Phil 2.05/0.96).
There are 35 'brain paced' skips but candidates_skipped_no_brain = 0. Those two fields contradict each other.
The 24h aggregates and the 48h skip table cover different windows, so their rates aren't directly comparable.
This summary has no per-coin 5m volume, flow ratio, buy ratio, drawdown or est_cost_pct, so the rule ideas can't be tested from it. Export per-coin rows for the Nov 10 review.

The cost model is unclear. 9.8% on a $10 buy points to fixed fees (priority fee, bribe, account rent) rather than pool impact. Log fixed and size-dependent costs separately so other position sizes can be simulated.
The 'other' skip reason (10 coins, 0 ran) needs a real label.
BASKET was logged as MIGRATED at 0.07h old, though a 'too new / sniping' filter exists. Check that the age filter is applied the same way at every stage.

daily_reviews.summary: No edge yet. All 276 settled coins lost money after costs under the simple plan: -6.4% average net. Every setup was negative: FINAL_STRETCH -3.6% (n=45), MIGRATED -5.1% (n=193), DIP -16.1% (n=38). Before costs the simple plan made roughly +3% overall and about +6% on FINAL_STRETCH. The ~9.7% round-trip cost on a $10 buy wipes that out, which is the same thing the 22 real trades showed: $18.83 of the $25.79 loss was fees and slippage. The sample is far too small to trust a 3–6% gross edge. Payoffs swing from +50% to -20%, so the error bar on 45 FINAL_STRETCH coins is about ±9 points. Repeat logs of the same coin also make the overall n look bigger than it is. Only the negative after-cost result is solid. The brain logged zero would-buys, so nobody can say yet whether it picks better than it passes. That missing data is the main thing to fix before Nov 10.
findings: Costs decide the result. Average round-trip cost is 9.7% of a $10 buy (FINAL_STRETCH 10.0, MIGRATED 9.6, DIP 9.6). Before costs: all coins about +3.3%, FINAL_STRETCH about +6.4%, MIGRATED about +4.5%, DIP about -6.5%. After costs every group is negative. At this size, fees are a bigger problem than coin picking.

DIP is clearly the worst setup: n=38, 10.5% ran, 2.6% hit 2x, median peak 1.10x, net -16.1%, and still negative before costs. The other setups ran 29–38% of the time. Four runners out of 38 is a small number, but the gap is large and DIP is the one setup that looks broken on this sample.
FINAL_STRETCH did best: n=45, 37.8% ran, 26.7% hit 2x, median peak 1.37x, net -3.6%. It still loses after costs, and with n=45 the gross number can't be told apart from zero.
MIGRATED is most of the sample: n=193, 29.5% ran, 20.7% hit 2x, net -5.1%. That is close to the overall average, so nothing stands out yet.

The checklist and the brain don't separate winners from losers on this metric. Checklist-failed coins (n=138): 28.3% ran, 22.5% hit 2x, net -6.2%. Coins that cleared the checklist and reached the brain (n=138): 28.3% ran, 15.9% hit 2x, net -6.5%, and they dumped more often (60.1% vs 52.2%). The rejected coins did no worse. Hard lines still stay where they are, because the -20% simulated stop probably hides the rug losses they exist to avoid (see data_issues).

Two of the top runners were FINAL_STRETCH coins under $20k market cap that the brain passed on. Pnut at $19.7k peaked at 9.48x in 25 minutes. Fug at $14.7k peaked at 7.27x in 33 minutes. Two coins are anecdotes, not a pattern. They are only a reason to compare low-cap FINAL_STRETCH coins against the rest.

PUMPCHAN (same CA) fills 3 of the 5 top-runner slots: 18.3x, 7.8x and 7.0x from logs at $270k, $1.15M and $1.32M. Its time to high was 322–353 minutes, right at the end of the 6h window, so the real peak was probably later. Every time it was blocked by the checklist.

The 48h skips mostly earn their keep. Top 10 over 25%: 42 blocked, 6 ran (14%), 35 dumped (83%). RugCheck danger: 27 blocked, 3 ran, 23 dumped (85%), with dumped examples falling to 0.01–0.02x, which means rugs. Flow below pace: 37 blocked, 3 ran (8%), 25 dumped. Falling knife (code): 17 blocked, 3 ran, 13 dumped. Thin 5m volume: 10 blocked, 1 ran, 7 dumped. Each of these ran less than the 28% base rate.

Some skips block about the base rate of runners and don't show they help. Too new / sniping: 27 blocked, 8 ran (30%), 19 dumped. Brain paced: 31 blocked, 7 ran (23%), 23 dumped. Near the high / chasing: 28 blocked, 6 ran (21%), 19 dumped. Bundles and dev-share blocks also sit near base rate, but n is only 13–17. None of this is evidence to loosen them, only evidence they are neutral on this small sample.

About two-thirds of the coins that reached 1.5x also reached 2x: 19.2% hit 2x against 28.3% that ran. Selling everything at 1.5x may cut off the right tail, but this can only be tested with order-aware price paths, not peak-only numbers.

Brain usage was 413 calls in 48h with 0 plan-limit hits, 0 candidates skipped for no brain and 0 stop reviews without a brain. The plan limit isn't binding. Only Trencher's own pace cap is, and it blocked 31 coins.
rule_ideas: Turn DIP off: setup == DIP → no entry. Alternatively allow it only if 5m volume ≥ 1h average pace and buy ratio ≥ 0.55. Test whether the filtered DIP subset gets above zero before costs. If it doesn't, drop DIP for good.

Cost gate: enter only if estimated round-trip cost_pct ≤ 5%. Re-run the simple plan by cost bucket (<5%, 5–10%, >10%) and at larger notional sizes ($25 and $50 against pool liquidity). This shows whether the gross edge survives once fixed fees are a smaller share.

FINAL_STRETCH with mcap < $25k and 5m volume ≥ $10k against FINAL_STRETCH with mcap ≥ $25k. Report n, the share that hit 2x, and net after costs. Pnut and Fug are what prompted this split, not proof of it.
MIGRATED, V6 recon band: mcap $70k–$11M, age ≤ 12h, 5m volume ≥ $10k, flow ratio (5m volume ÷ (1h volume / 12)) ≥ 1.0, buy ratio ≥ 0.5. Compare against the rest of MIGRATED.

Exit-plan test on the same entries, order-aware: (a) sell all at 1.5x or -20%; (b) sell initials at 2x, trail the rest by 30% off the high, hard stop -30%; (c) break-even stop after 1.3x. Only worth doing if the logs keep the full sample path.
Checklist-pass AND brain conviction ≥ 6 against checklist-pass AND brain PASS. This only works once the brain logs a hypothetical BUY and conviction in watch-only mode.

Look at 'too new / sniping' again on the full week, split by setup and mcap. If the blocked coins keep running at or above base rate (currently 30%), test entries at age ≥ 15 min with checklist passed, instead of a flat age block. Never snipe brand-new pairs.
Keep the hard lines out of the test (top 10, RugCheck danger, dev share, bundles, hack names). Check them only on rug rate, the share of coins with worst_x < 0.1, not on simple-plan net.
data_issues: would_buy n=0 for 24h while 138 coins reached the brain. Either the watch-only prompt stops the brain from saying BUY, or hypothetical buys aren't being logged. The main question for the week (do would-buys beat passes?) can't be answered until this is fixed. Log the decision and conviction as if trading were on.

checklist_failed and brain_passed are both exactly 138. That could be a coincidence or a labeling or join bug. 'brain_passed' is also unclear: does it mean the brain said PASS, or the coin passed through to the brain? Confirm which.

The same coin gets logged more than once: PUMPCHAN takes 3 of the 5 top-runner rows. Repeat entries inflate n and make the samples look more independent than they are. Deduplicate by CA (first qualifying log, or one per cooldown window) before Nov 10.

Skip reasons overlap: Manlet appears under both bundles and too-new, Jimmies under both falling-knife buckets, enu under chasing and no-higher-low. Skip counts can't be added up. Give each coin one primary reason, plus a list of all reasons.

The -20% simulated stop is probably too kind to rugs. Dumped examples hit 0.00–0.02x (Valueless, BTC, JENSEN, DONJENSEN, GPUBREAK, Pumpcat). If a gap between samples is booked at -20% instead of the next real price, losses are understated and the brain/checklist comparison is biased. Book the next sampled price, and log the sampling interval.
The 6h window cuts off late peaks: PUMPCHAN topped out 322–353 minutes in. max_x is a floor for slow runners, and a 6h close can miss late rugs.
Skips use a 48h window while setup and stage stats use 24h. Put both on the same window.

'brain paced' blocked 31 coins in 48h, yet candidates_skipped_no_brain is 0 and plan_limit_hits is 0. Trencher's own pace cap is blocking coins without being counted as a brain skip. Since there's plan headroom, loosen the cap during watch-only so every candidate gets a brain decision.
The 'other' skip bucket (13 blocked, 1 ran, 12 dumped) has no named reason. Log the actual reason text.

'ran' and 'dumped' aren't defined in the output. FINAL_STRETCH sums to exactly 100% (37.8 + 62.2) while the overall total is 84.5%. Write down the thresholds and whether a coin can be both (ran, then dumped).
The same symbol shows up under different CAs (POORGOAT ×2, 4CHAN ×2). Group by CA, not symbol, and add vamp detection to the analysis.

Not logged but needed for the rule tests: per-coin flow ratio, buy ratio, liquidity, cost-model inputs (fixed vs slippage split) and full price paths for order-aware exit tests. Check these fields are saved for every logged coin.
